{"body":"Part of #35 (section 3, enhancement 1).

## The defect (a cost, not a bug)

`Logger.Debug($"enemy {id} at {x},{y}")` builds the whole string — formats the numbers, allocates — and only THEN does the level filter discard it. The diary analogy: you spend the evening writing the page, and the editor throws it away unread. You still spent the evening.

At ~390 call sites this is invisible until something logs per-entity: one world bake in *Witch v Necromancer* formatted ~80,000 messages nobody would ever read. Measured:

| 200k discarded `Logger.Debug($"…")` calls | time | allocations |
|---|---|---|
| before | 51 ms | 37 MB |
| after | **0.15 ms** | **0** |

Proven two ways beyond the numbers: a `Logger.Debug($"never built {new Boom()}")` where `Boom.ToString()` throws did NOT throw (the hole is never evaluated), and a real seed run at a suppressed level formatted 2 lines instead of 191.

## The fix (proven in the game, ready to port)

C#'s interpolated string handler pattern: the compiler hands the handler the *pieces*, the handler checks the level FIRST and only assembles if enabled. The level rides in the TYPE — `Message<TLevel>` ref-struct handler with `ILogLevelTag` static-abstract tags (`AtDebug`/`AtInfo`/`AtWarning`/`AtError`) — so ONE handler body serves all four levels and the disabled path JITs to a static field read plus a compare.

- All ~390 call sites compile unchanged (handler overload for `$"…"`, plain `string` overload kept for the rest; `"literal " + $"interp {x}"` concatenations bind to the string overload and stay eager, correctly — there is nothing to defer).
- `MinimumLevel` / `IsEnabled` become public lock-free reads for the hot path.

Reference implementation: `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `Gmtk2026.Core/MonoDreams/foundation/State/Logger.cs`.

## Delivery

- [ ] Port the handler overloads + level tags into `MonoDreams/foundation/State/Logger.cs`
- [ ] `Initialize` / `UpdateGameTime` / `Shutdown` and the OUTPUT FORMAT stay byte-identical — the line format is a parsing contract (replay/verification tooling greps it)
- [ ] Test: a throwing `ToString()` inside a suppressed-level interpolation does not throw; an enabled-level line is byte-identical to before; both call forms compile against the new surface unchanged

## Deliberately out of scope

The game also defaults Release builds to `Warning` — that is a policy choice in the game's `GameRoot`, not the engine. This PR only makes suppressed logs free; what each game suppresses stays its own business.

**Value on its own:** every MonoDreams game currently pays full formatting for every suppressed line, forever — and the workaround people reach for is deleting useful logging, which is strictly worse.
","comments":[],"labels":[],"title":"foundation: Logger interpolated-string handlers — a suppressed log line must cost nothing"}
